status: MEASURED — and it closes the score-function route on dimensional grounds
criterion: P-A' / plan 2.42. Frozen: C0 phi dynamic range; R r(32)>=0.5 or 'not estimable'; C1' descriptive cos(path,teach); SELF batch-vs-single gate.

design.phi: path J2 = mean over slot tokens of [log p(slot+ | x, y) - log p(slot- | x, y)] teacher-forced on the model's OWN continuation y, in NATS
design.decomposition: grad E_y[phi] = E_y[grad phi] (pathwise) + E_y[(phi-b) grad log p^(y)] (score term); both terms measured on the SAME 32 rollouts

C0.note: 1.33 nat total / 0.43 nat within-context dynamic range, versus 0.0405 +- 0.01 for the saturated judge in plan 2.40: the scale problem is fixed

R.verdict: FAILS the frozen gate (r(32) < 0.5). The curve is FLAT in K, so the Spearman-Brown r(K)=K/(K+K0) form does not hold and K*=1424 is not a usable extrapolation: the noise is not independent across rollouts.

verdict: The score term is NOT estimable at K=32 (r=0.022, flat in K) and it is NOT a small correction (26x the pathwise norm). So the on-policy functional's derivative is dominated by a term we cannot measure, while the measurable part (pathwise, |g|=25.2) is only 0.42-aligned with the teacher-forced gradient of the same construct. Both facts are needed: the measure change is real (0.42, not 1.0), and its main carrier is not accessible by sampling.
method_note: The flat r(K) is a dimensional statement, not a sample-size one: per-rollout score vectors live in 294,912 dimensions and are mutually near-orthogonal, so averaging needs K ~ dim rather than K ~ 10^2. Refusing to tune here means refusing the estimator class, not adding rollouts. What remains closed-form-friendly is the pathwise term, whose only randomness is the trajectory (phi sd 0.43 nat within context, so 32 trajectories give SE ~ 0.076 nat).
